content.user_title: Manage Google Keep Notes with gws
content.value_statement: Managing Google Keep resources from an AI workflow requires precise CLI commands and API parameters. This skill guides structured note, attachment, and permission operations.
actual_capabilities: Create new Google Keep notes through the gws CLI.
Retrieve individual notes and list paginated note collections.
Delete notes when the authenticated caller has the OWNER role.
Discover note, media, and permission methods with CLI help.
Inspect required parameters, types, and defaults before API calls.
Download available attachment media in supported MIME types.
limitations: The gws CLI and its Google authentication setup must already be available.
The adjacent gws-shared skill supplies global flags and security guidance.
Note deletion is immediate, irreversible, and restricted to owners.
Attachment downloads depend on media availability and the requested MIME type.

use_cases.title: Organize Personal Notes
use_cases.description: Create and retrieve Keep notes from a guided command workflow.

use_cases.title: Review Shared Note Access
use_cases.description: Inspect available permission operations before managing collaboration settings.

use_cases.title: Process Note Collections
use_cases.description: List notes across pages and preserve continuation tokens for later requests.

prompt_templates.title: List My Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to list my Google Keep notes. Inspect the method schema first and explain any pagination fields.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Google Keep note creation request for this content: {note_content}. Inspect required parameters before proposing the command.

prompt_templates.title: Download an Attachment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me download attachment {attachment_name} from note {note_name}. Verify media parameters and explain MIME type constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Paginated Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe workflow to review all Keep notes, continue through page tokens, and identify permission operations without deleting anything.

output_examples.input: List my Keep notes and explain how to continue after the first page.
output_examples.output: The response includes up to the requested page size. Use the returned next page token in the following request to continue.

output_examples.input: Delete a shared note that I own.
output_examples.output: Ownership must be confirmed before deletion. Deletion is immediate, cannot be undone, and removes collaborator access.

output_examples.input: Download an attachment from a Keep note.
output_examples.output: Inspect the media download schema, request attachment media, and choose an available MIME type. Unsupported media requests return a bad-request response.

best_practices: Inspect each method schema before constructing parameters or request bodies.
Preserve opaque page tokens exactly when continuing a list operation.
Confirm ownership and user intent before any irreversible note deletion.
anti_patterns: Do not guess parameter names or types without checking the method schema.
Do not alter, decode, or reuse pagination tokens for unrelated requests.
Do not delete notes without confirming ownership, collaborators, and irreversible impact.

faq.question: What setup does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the gws CLI, Google authentication, and the generated gws-shared prerequisite skill.

faq.question: Can it create Google Keep notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the note creation method and directs the agent to inspect its schema before use.

faq.question: Can it list every note?
faq.answer: It supports paginated listing. Continue requests with the opaque next page token until no token remains.

faq.question: Can deleted notes be restored?
faq.answer: No. The documented delete operation removes a note immediately and cannot be undone.

faq.question: Who can delete a note?
faq.answer: The authenticated caller must have the OWNER role on that note.

faq.question: Can it download every attachment format?
faq.answer: No. Downloads depend on media availability and the MIME types supported for the attachment.
